prediction.likelyOutcome: Speedy's claims (contract balance, unjust enrichment, lien foreclosure) are likely to fail or yield only a nominal recovery given strong, contemporaneous evidence of poor performance, missed deadlines, and overbilling supporting Windsor's termination for cause. Windsor should recover on its breach-of-contract counterclaim for cost of completion in the mid-five figures, and has a real but uncertain shot at slander-of-title damages — clearly for the ~$3,960 bond cost, and more speculatively for the much larger financing-cost claim, which depends on proving malice and on firmer damages proof than appears in this record.

outcome.description: After a two-day bench trial the court found for Windsor, awarded it $44,300 (the amount it had paid Speedy) plus prejudgment and postjudgment interest on its breach-of-contract counterclaim and $3,960 on its slander-of-title counterclaim (bond premiums), a total of $48,260, voided Speedy's $66,000 mechanics lien and denied Speedy's claims. The Second District affirmed.
